traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Costaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; margins entire; veins pinnate; blades lanceolate, oblanceolate, oblong or ovate; plants hermaphrodite; ovary inferior; stems herbaceous; flowers zygomorphic; perianth sepals and petals; fruit capsule, nut or achene; parts of each whorl 3; stamens 1; carpels 3. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Costaceae: flowers very irregular, the corolla's median member largest, the stamens reduced to one fertile and the rest joined in a showy lip. That lip below two smaller petals is drawn as an orchid's lip is: zygomorphy labellate.

traits.inflorescence.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 124, 125, family Costaceae: inflorescence raceme, terminal; read as "raceme".
